facts.claim: PARTIES/STRUCTURE: Equity Purchase Agreement dated April 29, 2026. Buyer = MARA USA Corporation (Delaware corp, subsidiary of MARA Holdings, Inc.). Sellers = Ohio River Partners Holdco LLC ('ORPH', direct wholly-owned sub of FIP) and Ohio River Partners Finance LLC ('ORPF', direct wholly-owned sub of ORPH). MARA Holdings is a party solely for Articles V, IX and X; FTAI Infrastructure Inc. (FIP) is a party solely for Articles V, IX and X and Sections 2.5, 6.10, 6.16 and 6.20. It is an EQUITY sale: Buyer purchases 100% of the issued and outstanding LLC membership interests of Long Ridge Energy & Power LLC ('LRE&P'), a Delaware LLC and indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of FIP.
facts.source: FIP 8-K Item 1.01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1899883/000114036126018033/ef20071666_8k.htm ; corroborated by MARA 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000119312526193982/d54802d8k.htm

facts.claim: ASSETS SOLD: Long Ridge is a vertically integrated power and gas company: 485 MW combined-cycle gas plant in Hannibal, Ohio (MARA 8-K: 'expected to increase to 505 MW nameplate capacity in H2 2026'; MARA PR footnote: 'Currently authorized to sell 485 MW'; the PJM IMM describes it as a 522 MW CCGT), working interests in natural gas production wells, and ~1,600 acres along the Ohio River. MARA already operates a co-located data center at the Long Ridge site (Hannibal campus, acquired from Arkon Energy Nov 2024).
facts.source: FIP PR Ex-99.1 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1899883/000114036126018033/ef20071666_ex99-1.htm ; MARA 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000119312526193982/d54802d8k.htm ; IMM comment https://www.monitoringanalytics.com/filings/2026/IMM_Comment_Docket_No_EC26-92_20260529.pdf

facts.claim: PRICE/CONSIDERATION: Base purchase price $1.512 billion per FIP's 8-K ('base purchase price of $1.512 billion, subject to certain customary adjustments'); FIP PR headlines 'approximately $1.52 billion before closing adjustments'; MARA states 'approximately $1.5 billion' total transaction value 'including the assumption of at least $785 million of debt, backstopped by a bridge loan from Barclays'. All-cash equity purchase; no stock consideration, no earnout. At closing $20 million goes into escrow 'to secure and serve as the sole course of recovery for any post-closing purchase price adjustments in favor of Buyer.'
facts.source: FIP 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1899883/000114036126018033/ef20071666_8k.htm ; FIP PR Ex-99.1 (same accession) ; MARA PR Ex-99.1 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000119312526193982/d54802dex991.htm

facts.claim: CLOSING CONDITIONS (FIP 8-K narrative): '(a) the absence of any law, regulation, order, or injunction that makes the Transaction illegal...; (b) the making or obtaining of all required filings, consents and approvals under applicable law, including (i) the receipt of authorization from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission under Section 203 of the Federal Power Act, as amended, (ii) the expiration of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended and (iii) solely with respect to the Railroad Agreements, authorization by the Surface Transportation Board pursuant to 49 C.F.R. § 1180; and (c) in the case of Buyer's obligations..., (i) no Material Adverse Effect... having occurred and that is continuing as of the closing...; and receipt of consents from certain counterparties under certain material contracts.' Plus reps-accuracy and covenant-performance conditions.
facts.source: FIP 8-K Item 1.01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1899883/000114036126018033/ef20071666_8k.htm

facts.claim: CLOSING CONDITIONS (EPA text, Art. VII): Sec 7.1(a) No Order; Sec 7.1(b): '(i) The filings, consents and approvals required to be made or obtained under applicable Laws in order to consummate the Closing as set forth in Section 7.1(b) of the Disclosure Letter, shall have been made or obtained, and (ii) the waiting period under the HSR Act shall have expired or been terminated.' Buyer-only conditions (Sec 7.2): reps true (MAE standard), covenants performed, 'No Material Adverse Effect... occurred and be continuing', officer certificates, and 7.2(e): 'The COC Amendment shall have been obtained and shall be in full force and effect, and the lenders under the EB-5 Loan Agreement shall have waived any default... resulting from any change of control' ('COC Conditions'). NO financing condition: FIP 8-K states verbatim 'Buyer's obligation to consummate the Transaction is not subject to a financing condition.' PJM appears ZERO times in the agreement — there is no PJM approval condition.
facts.source: Equity Purchase Agreement, Exhibit 10.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000119312526193982/d54802dex101.htm (also filed as Ex-10.1 to FIP 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1899883/000114036126018033/ef20071666_ex10-1.htm)

facts.claim: TERMINATION (EPA Art. VIII): (a) mutual consent; (b) either party on a final non-appealable order prohibiting the sale; (c)/(d) either Buyer or Sellers 'at any time after November 30, 2026 (the Outside Date)' if not consummated (not available to a party whose own covenant failure caused the delay) — BUT if on the Outside Date all conditions are satisfied EXCEPT the Sec 7.1(b) regulatory condition, neither may terminate 'until after June 30, 2027'; also tolled until 3 business days after the end of a commenced-but-incomplete debt-financing 'Marketing Period'; breach terminations with cure rights; and (e) Sellers may terminate if all conditions are met, Sellers give irrevocable ready-willing-able notice, and Buyer fails to close by the earlier of the Outside Date or 3 business days after the notice.
facts.source: Equity Purchase Agreement Sections 8.1-8.2, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000119312526193982/d54802dex101.htm

facts.claim: TERMINATION FEE: One-way, Buyer-pays-Sellers 'Reverse Termination Fee' (EPA Sec 8.3) of $75,000,000, payable within 5 business days, ONLY in financing-failure scenarios: termination by Sellers under 8.1(d)(ii)/8.1(e) 'in the circumstance where Buyer's failure to consummate the Closing is due solely to the fact that the Debt Financing or Alternative Debt Financing is not funded to Buyer in accordance with the Debt Commitment Letter', or by Buyer under 8.1(c)(i) when Sellers could then have so terminated. MARA Holdings (Buyer Parent) 'absolutely, unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees payment of the Termination Fee'. No termination fee is payable by Sellers/FIP in any direction. Otherwise post-termination liability only for willful and material breach or Fraud.
facts.source: Equity Purchase Agreement Sections 8.3 and Buyer Parent guarantee, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000119312526193982/d54802dex101.htm ; FIP 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1899883/000114036126018033/ef20071666_8k.htm

unresolved: The purchase agreement exhibit IS public (Ex-10.1 to both 8-Ks), but the Disclosure Letter and schedules are omitted (Reg S-K 601(a)(5)) — so the exact enumerated list of 'required filings, consents and approvals' in Section 7.1(b) of the Disclosure Letter is not publicly verifiable; FERC 203 / HSR / STB are confirmed only via the 8-K narratives. MARA's copy also has confidential redactions (601(b)(10)(iv)).
HSR status: no public confirmation found that the HSR waiting period has expired or been terminated as of 2026-07-20.

FERC Docket EC26-92-000 outcome: no order found through 2026-07-20; whether FERC will impose the PJM-market-commitment condition requested by the IMM is unresolved. FERC's eLibrary was not directly queried (fetched sources only).

Price reconciliation: FIP 8-K says base purchase price $1.512B; FIP PR says ~$1.52B 'transaction value'; MARA says ~$1.5B 'including the assumption of certain debt' (at least $785M). The precise equity-vs-enterprise bridge (how the $1.16B Long Ridge debt paydown nets against the base price) is not broken out in public documents.

Which specific FIP parent-level debt (~$300M) will be repaid is not named in the April 30 PR; the July 1 Jefferson bridge loan mandates prepayment from asset-sale proceeds but is not explicitly tied to Long Ridge in the filing.

Railroad Agreements (East Ohio Valley Railway) were signing-date term-sheet only ('negotiate and finalize in good faith'); no public update on their execution or the STB authorization status was found.
The 'Marketing Period' definition (which can toll outside-date termination) sits in redacted/undisclosed portions; its exact mechanics were not extracted.
MARA's Q2 2026 10-Q (not yet filed as of 2026-07-20) and FIP's Q2 filings would be the next authoritative status checkpoints.

synthesis.rationale: The skeptic's $1.59B pref claim is CONFIRMED by the Q1-2026 10-Q: RailCo Series A redemption value $1,417.5M (per-unit $1,417.49 x 1.0M units; $1.4B stated liquidation preference + $64.4M PIK) + Series B change-of-control redemption $182.0M = $1,599.5M at 2026-03-31 - the $1.59B figure matches an early-2026 measurement date and the stack PIKs ~10%/yr (stepping to 12%/14%). It is invisible to casual SoP work because balance-sheet carrying value is only $1,123.2M. Consequence: the recorded thesis mechanism (de-lever via Long Ridge sale -> $9 analyst SoP) cannot occur. Even a CLEAN close at generous multiples (Railroad 10x, Jefferson 12x, Repauno at full book) leaves mechanical common equity at -$744.5M (-$6.30/share); $9 requires +$1,063M. The catalyst is real and likely fires (no financing condition, $75M RTF + parent guarantee + specific performance, notes consent completed, 5/6 FERC precedents approved, 180-day clock ~11/4/26), but it delivers a sentiment re-rate to ~$5.60 at best - 38% below target - and the 40%-probability branch is a close followed by proceeds redeployment into acquisitions (PR says so verbatim; Fortress external-manager fee structure on assets rewards exactly that) while $149M/yr of pref PIK keeps transferring value away from a common that already has negative book equity. EV $4.56/share vs $4.03 tape is only +13% with 45% of that EV riding on the market ignoring negative mechanical NAV, and the EPA's regulatory tail (no termination until 6/30/2027 if only 7.1(b) is open) means an unresolved seat can be dragged past the sleeve's 2026 window with no exit ramp. The recorded floor ($3.90) is also falsified: 52wk low is now $3.85 and a deal-break trades to ~$2.90. This is a thesis-broken exit, not edge-gone: the event edge exists, but the underwritten payoff path was arithmetically impossible from day one.

verdicts.strongest_objection: The Scenario A/B asset side rests on an unverified ~$600M net-cash bridge that the evidence pack itself flags as unresolved ("Whether the $1.52B base purchase price is an enterprise-value construct (buyer assumes/repays the ~$1.146B Long Ridge debt) or equity proceeds to FIP"). MARA's own PR language — "approximately $1.5 billion... including the assumption of at least $785 million of debt" — supports the enterprise reading, under which net cash to FIP is only ~$366M-$727M, short of the $530M of mandated uses ($230M Jefferson bridge prepay contractually required from asset sales per the 7/1/26 credit agreement + $300M announced parent paydown). That erases the $70M residual cash in Scenario A (deepening mechanical NAV deficit by up to ~$2/sh) and undercuts Scenario B's $4.20 (a cash-strapped close, not a redeploy-flush one). Second-order generosities all lean the same way: (1) the 0.45-weight re-rate to $5.60 is priced against a tape that FADED from $4.43 (07-06) to $4.09 (07-20 IBKR snapshot) as the close approaches — the market is discounting the deal, not building a re-rate, and the $5.83 52wk-midpoint anchor includes pre-9.75%-term-loan, pre-RailCo-pref periods; (2) claims are measured at 3/31 for a Q4 close while the RailCo pref PIKs $27.0M + $5.2M accretion per quarter (add ~$65-100M, another $0.55-0.85/sh of deficit; issuer take-out is at the GREATER of liquidation value or 1.5x = $1.5B per the 10-K); (3) the $2.90 floor (0.75x 52wk low) is high for a break that lands on the DRP DB $108.3M maturity 11/30/26 with $37.9M unrestricted cash, -$69.4M Q1 operating cash flow, and an MD&A whose 12-month liquidity conclusion explicitly depends on this sale — going-concern doubt argues $2.00-2.50, and no RTF is payable on a regulatory block (fee is financing-failure-only per EPA Sec 8.3); (4) the "5 of 6 FERC precedent dockets approved" close-probability support is asserted in the synthesis but appears nowhere in the evidence contract, and HSR status is explicitly unverified. Crucially, every one of these attacks makes the synthesis MORE bearish, not less: the load-bearing arithmetic is confirmed (claims $3,778.5M, assets $3,034M, residual -$744.5M = -$6.30/sh on 118.164M shares; pref stack $1,599.5M ties to the Q1-2026 10-Q; EV math 4.563 and probs sum 1.00 both check). The $9 target is arithmetically impossible under every reading, so EXIT_THESIS_BROKEN survives a fortiori — no load-bearing number fails in the direction that would rescue the seat.
